Subject: Rebalance request — service bands + SOW edits

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Mednexa has reviewed the draft MSA and Order Form and we want to propose a rebalancing of the service bands across Phase 1/Phase 2 to better align cost with our expected ramp. High level asks: 

- Move 40% of committed throughput from Band B into Band A for Q1–Q2 of the contract, with lower per-token price for Band A up to the bumped capacity.
- Add an optional Phase 2 onboarding SOW (90 days) with a freeze period for changes during initial production (we included a draft scope).
- Clarify rollback/exit financials if we drop below minimum monthly usage in month 7–12.

I've attached our internal cost model and a redline of the SOW (SOW_revised_20260728.pdf, cost-breakdown.xls). For legal redlines to the MSA we can share one more doc after you confirm the commercial approach.

Can you loop in the relevant Redwood folks (legal + commercial) so we can get an estimate of the commercial impact and a proposed change order draft? We hope to close this before our board meeting on Aug 10.

Thanks — Susan

--
Susan Kim
VP, Cloud Integrations | Mednexa Therapeutics

Susan — thanks for the clear summary and for attaching the model. Looping in Irene (legal) and Laura (commercial/ops) to take this through a coordinated change-order path.

Quick thoughts from me:
- Commercially the ask to shift 40% from Band B -> A should be doable as a timebound repricing (Q1–Q2) with a phased ramp clause. We'll need to create a short-term addendum to the Order Form that pins the effective dates and the per-token floor.
- For the SOW freeze during initial production, we can capture that as an Exhibit with change-control steps and a 30-day review window for new feature requests.
- Rollback/exit: Laura — can you run a prorated charge matrix for the ramp-down scenario (months 7–12) so we can propose acceptable thresholds? Irene — can you call out any MSA language that would block a timeboxed repricing or complicate the change order?

I'll consolidate inputs and draft a change-order skeleton (Order Form addendum + SOW exhibit) once we have answers from legal and ops. Targeting a first draft by end of day tomorrow so Susan has something before your board date.

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-07-29T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rebalance request — service bands + SOW edits

Thanks Mateo — reviewed Susan's ask. High-level legal guidance below; I added inline comments to redlines_MSA_v3.docx (attached).

1) Timeboxed repricing — acceptable with the following controls:
   - Explicit effective window (e.g., 2026-08-01 to 2027-02-01).
   - Auto-reversion clause unless both parties sign an extension prior to window end.

2) Rollback/exit financials — we should avoid open-ended clawbacks. Propose:
   - If monthly committed usage falls >30% below the committed baseline for two consecutive months between months 7–12, client owes a prorated true-up equal to (committed - actual) * contracted rate for up to 2 months.
   - For persistence >3 months, escalate to commercial review for longer-term fee adjustments.

3) SOW freeze — acceptable if we include an explicit change-control process and an exception for security/critical bug fixes.

4) IP/data language — confirm that the phased deployment doesn't introduce any new data residency requirements. (Susan: if you require additional residency constraints we need to know now.)

Laura — please share the prorate matrix. Once I have the numbers I will translate the clauses into redline language and return a tracked MSA+OrderForm addendum.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_MSA_v3.docx (inline comments)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-07-29T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rebalance request — service bands + SOW edits

Team / Susan — attaching the cost-breakdown.xls with two scenarios: (A) timeboxed repricing for Q1–Q2 with fee smoothing, and (B) permanent band reallocation. Summary below:

- Scenario A (preferred): 40% shift Band B -> A for 6 months. Estimated revenue impact: ~6% ARR dilution in year 1, but reduces ramp friction and accelerates go-live.
- Scenario B: permanent reallocation increases long-term exposure by ~15% but gives Mednexa lower unit economics.

Proposed commercial compromise: approve Scenario A via a Change Order + Exhibit that auto-reverts on 2027-02-01 unless extended. For rollback true-up, use Irene's proposed thresholds.

Susan — can you confirm comfortable with the temporary vs permanent tradeoff? If temporary is acceptable I'll produce the Order Form addendum and a redlined Exhibit for the SOW freeze (with acceptance gates).

Laura Bennett
Commercial Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: cost-breakdown.xls (scenarios A & B), fees_matrix.pdf
